title: No, That's Not a Software Factory — Ryan Cooke, WorkOS
talk_summary: WorkOS built a software factory (TARS for agent interaction, Horizon for orchestration) but found raw code output indistinguishable from engineers using Claude Code locally, so they shifted to encoding engineering processes (hilltop PRDs, Linear ticket dependencies, webhooks) into the factory and measuring outcomes not PR counts. Their key leverage was an internal MCP gateway ('context engine') that connects internal systems with tool descriptions telling agents how to navigate them, which became useful company-wide.

takeaways.technique: Internal MCP gateway with tool-description orientation
takeaways.what_they_do: A single MCP server connects all internal systems (Snowflake semantic tables, Linear, docs) and its tool descriptions explain what each table/tool contains and when to query it, giving agents orientation on how the company organizes information.
takeaways.evidence_quote: invest in an internal MCP gateway server that both connects all your tools, has descriptions that can tell the agent how to use those tools

takeaways.what_they_do: TARS subscribes to Linear/GitHub webhooks; when a blocking ticket completes it automatically picks up the next dependent ticket, and between steps asks the agent to re-evaluate the project for missing tickets to keep the plan fresh.
takeaways.evidence_quote: TARS is getting webhooks on ticket completion, it can automatically pick up the next ticket in a cycle

takeaways.technique: Agent-seeded PRD/hilltop to beat the blank page
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's that blank page problem with writing. If you can come into a document that already has information

takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly reject PR-count/percent-AI-code metrics because they can disguise whether the factory works, and instead track feature delivery acceleration, defect rate, time-to-recovery, and engineer adoption of the cloud sandbox.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Percentage of PRs or number of PRs may be lying in overall increase in PRs

takeaways.technique: Own the sandbox to capture session telemetry for self-improvement
takeaways.what_they_do: They are moving off sandbox-as-a-service to own the infra so they can see full session data, then point agents at sessions to find skill gaps, obsolete skills, and where agents made mistakes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can actually point agents at sessions and see where are the gaps and how people are using our factory

takeaways.technique: Process-embedded factory, not just code generation
takeaways.what_they_do: They found a sandbox+agent+prompt+PR loop was 'pretty indistinguishable' from engineers using Claude Code locally, and got gains only after embedding their actual engineering rituals (PRD review, ticket dependencies, triage) into the automation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It was actually pretty indistinguishable for us
